author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory at GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it by full name, all on one page and reachable by URL alone.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html answers with the specialty directory page.
Every specialty the clinic knows is listed by its stored name, exactly as stored in every language, neither translated nor re-cased.
Each veterinarian holding a specialty appears under it by first name then last name, for example "Helen Leary".
A veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each of them.
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed and names no veterinarian.
Every specialty and every holding veterinarian renders on one page, with no paging, however many veterinarians the clinic employs.
The page offers no way to add, change, or remove a veterinarian or a specialty.
No navigation entry and no link on any other page leads to the page.
The page carries the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory that REQ-SYS-001 requires of every page.
The page's own wording follows the reader's language, with no hard-coded text and no language left partly translated, per REQ-LANG-001 and REQ-LANG-002.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged by the owner's decision).
A navigation entry or a link from any other page; the owner left a visible entry point to a possible follow-up request.
Searching or filtering specialties or veterinarians (NG-9).
A machine-readable form of the directory.
Any change to the veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001), and links from the directory to other pages.
notes: Judged cold against docs/prd.md: no contradiction, no pushback, no Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. NG-2 stands: the view is read-only, per intake line 1. NG-9 declines search; this page is an unfiltered listing, not a search, and carries no search or filter. A page without an entry point to it still carries REQ-SYS-001 navigation out of it; the owner's decision limits links to the page, not the shared navigation. Narrowest readings taken, per the owner's instruction, each recorded under docs/prd.md Open Questions: (1) no order is required for specialties or for veterinarians under one, so tests assert membership, not order; (2) a specialty no veterinarian holds is listed and names no veterinarian, with no requirement for an explicit marker either way; (3) no visible entry point. Vocabulary: Specialty Directory and Full Name added to docs/ubiquitous-language.md. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package (system-design.md Package Structure, Contracts, Specialty directory invariants, Scale and Load). Fresh ground: the codebase's first non-entity value object and first anti-corruption mapper, both sanctioned by architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog, so no ADR. Shape: package-private SpecialtyController reads SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository.findAll(), hands both to the static mapper SpecialtyDirectory.fromSpecialtiesAndVets, and returns view vets/specialtyDirectory. The inversion is a change of representation, so it leaves the bean (Logic Placement table). Inverting the vet list alone is wrong: it would lose a specialty no veterinarian holds. Basis: grep and file reads; the IntelliJ oracle was not connected, the weaker basis. grep confirmed @Cacheable and createCache appear only for the vets cache, and BaseEntity defines no equals.
integration_points: Boundary, repository, unit level: SpecialtyDirectoryTests crosses none; it uses real Vet and Specialty instances with ids set.

Boundary, repository, web level: SpecialtyControllerTests uses hand-written in-memory doubles of SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository, supplied through a @TestConfiguration import. No @MockitoBean: both interfaces are narrow enough to hand-write (testing-principles.md Mocking Policy).
Boundary, repository, persistence level: SpecialtyRepositoryTests uses the real repository on seeded H2 with @DataJpaTest and @AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE), as ClinicServiceTests does.
Boundary, framework transport: MockMvc through @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class), the sanctioned in-process harness, rendering the real template.
Binding, GET /specialties.html: the entry point binds no request parameter or form object, so no binding target exists and no @InitBinder is needed. The handler takes only Model.
Exposure (security-principles.md Widening the exposed surface): the route is open to any caller, per the baseline, and shows specialty names and veterinarian names that /vets.html already shows.

SpecialtyRepository: package-private interface extending the narrow Repository<Specialty, Integer> as VetRepository does, with a single read method in name order. No other package uses it (Design Principle 5).
VetController stays untouched, including its constructor, so REQ-VET-001 and VetControllerTests are unchanged (prd-entry non_goals).

SpecialtyDirectory and its nested Listing record: public, Listing holding the stored specialty name and holder Full Names, both lists through List.copyOf. Named caller for the widened visibility: PetClinicRuntimeHints, which registers both with public-method reflection for SpEL template access in a native image.

Template: vets/specialtyDirectory.html passes menu value 'specialties' to fragments/layout, so REQ-SYS-001 navigation renders with no item marked active; layout.html is not edited. It reuses the existing message keys specialties and vets, present in every bundle, so no bundle edit is expected. A new key would need all ten translated bundles.

patterns.description: lookup-value repository in name order; precedent for a repository on a type another entity references. Specialty stands to Vet as PetType stands to Pet.
narrow Spring Data Repository with @Transactional(readOnly = true) reads.
layout fragment use and th:text rendering.
view model as a change of representation lands in a mapper; naming from{Source}() per Language Realization Building Blocks.

risks.risk: Grouping by name or by Specialty object equality. BaseEntity defines no equals, so a cached Vet's Specialty never equals the repository's instance, and specialty names carry no unique constraint.
risks.mitigation: Match by Integer id with equals, per system-design.md Specialty directory invariants. Key nothing on the name. SpecialtyDirectoryTests covers two specialties sharing a name, and a holder whose Specialty is a different instance with the same id.

risks.risk: Adding an inverse @ManyToMany to Specialty. Eager fetch widens every vet load, lazy fails with open-in-view disabled, and the /vets serialization would recurse.
risks.mitigation: Specialty stays unchanged, per system-design.md Specialty directory invariants and Persistence (open-in-view line).

risks.risk: A getFullName() getter on Vet joins the JSON and XML output of /vets, a change the prd-entry non_goals exclude.
risks.mitigation: Package-private Vet.fullName(), not a bean property, per system-design.md Specialty directory invariants. VetTests covers it. vetList.html keeps its own concatenation.

risks.risk: Sharing the vets cache for specialties: a no-arg SpecialtyRepository read under @Cacheable("vets") takes the same key as VetRepository.findAll(), and one read then returns the other's type.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository is uncached, per its Contracts row. Open Question 5 records that the two reads can disagree after an out-of-band change.

risks.risk: Specialty directory page reads all specialties and all veterinarians unpaged (system-design.md Scale and Load, specialty directory row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: a stream over the veterinarians for each specialty; no index map and no pagination.

risks.risk: Stored names reach the page, and a specialty no veterinarian holds could break the row or gain a marker the request never asked for.
risks.mitigation: th:text only, never th:utext (security-principles.md Cross-site scripting). Render the stored name unchanged, with no message lookup or case transformation. An unheld specialty shows an empty holder cell, the narrowest reading in the prd-entry notes.

risks.risk: The native-image path is not exercised by the quality gate, so a missing reflection hint for the records would pass locally and fail at runtime.
risks.mitigation: Register both records in PetClinicRuntimeHints (system-design.md Specialty directory invariants).

notes: Five-signal foundational check: clear. No conflict with NG-2 or NG-9; the slice is one behavior. No ADR: the choices are catalog patterns or contained in this slice (adr-template When to Create an ADR). docs/system-design.md lacked Scale and Load; this dispatch added it from the doctor template with the slice's row. Docs changed: Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, VetRepository plus three new rows; Specialty directory invariants; package tree line; provenance sentence; Open Question 5. Order is not a requirement: specialties arrive in name order from the repository as a deterministic default, veterinarians under each in the order of the vet read, and tests assert membership per the prd-entry notes. Repository failures propagate to the standard error page; no timeouts or shutdown concerns are new. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records. Defect noted, not fixed: Specialty object references from Vet versus the identity rule in architecture-principles.md Domain Core are pre-existing, shared with Pet and PetType.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Widening the exposed surface: the change adds one route, GET /specialties.html (SpecialtyController.java:37 `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")`). It exposes only specialty names and vet full names to any caller, data already public through the open /vets.html and /vets routes, and it is read-only with no POST mapping in the controller. The open access is the demonstration baseline per docs/security-principles.md Standing Gaps. management exposure is unchanged (application.properties:21 `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=*`, not in the change set).

Mass assignment and request input: not introduced. `grep -F -e @RequestParam -e @PathVariable -e @ModelAttribute -e @RequestBody -e InitBinder -e Pageable` over SpecialtyController.java returned nothing, so the handler binds no request value and no disallow list applies. The `Model` parameter is output only, which also leaves no attacker-controlled input to validate and no cross-request identifier to trust.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.java:30 `List<Specialty> findAllByOrderByNameAsc();` is a derived query with no parameters. `grep -F -e @Query -e nativeQuery -e createQuery -e EntityManager` over vet/Specialty*.java returned nothing.

XSS and template evaluation: specialtyDirectory.html:18 `th:text="${listing.specialtyName}"` and :20 `th:text="${holder}"` render stored names through the escaping attribute. `grep -F -e th:utext -e '__$' -e '[(' -e '<script' -e th:href -e th:onclick` over the template returned nothing. The layout's `__${link}__` preprocessing (fragments/layout.html:31) is pre-existing, and the new template's 'specialties' argument is a literal that only feeds the `active==menu` comparison.

Resource selection and shell/file sinks: the view name is the fixed literal `vets/specialtyDirectory` (SpecialtyController.java:41). `grep -E 'Runtime|ProcessBuilder|exec\(|Files\.|JsonTypeInfo'` over vet/Specialty*.java returned nothing.

Serialization surface: Vet.java:79 `String fullName() {` is package-private and not a getter, so it does not join the /vets collection, and VetTests.java:35 `FULL_NAME_PROPERTY = "fullName"` is the test constant guarding that. PetClinicRuntimeHints adds only `MemberCategory.INVOKE_PUBLIC_METHODS` for SpecialtyDirectory and Listing, with no Java serialization hint, so the deserialization row stays at its baseline.

Resource use: the unpaged page is required by the PRD (docs/prd.md:133, all of them render on one page with no paging). Input size is bounded because the application has no write path: `grep -rn -F -e specialtyRepository. -e vetRepository.save -e addSpecialty(` over src/main/java found only the read at SpecialtyController.java:40 and the Vet.java:70 definition, with no caller. No request value influences result size. Vet specialties load eagerly (Vet.java:47 `@ManyToMany(fetch = FetchType.EAGER)`), so rendering hits no closed session, consistent with spring.jpa.open-in-view=false (application.properties:11). SpecialtyDirectory's immutable records are built per request and SpecialtyController holds only final repository fields, so no shared mutable state is added.

Secrets and logging: `grep -i -E 'password|secret|token|api[_-]?key|credential'` over the new production files and template returned nothing, nor did `grep -F -e System.out -e System.err -e printStackTrace -e log.` over vet/Specialty*.java. The change adds no exception message that could reach the error page.

Supply chain: build.gradle, pom.xml and gradle/ have no diff (`git diff --stat` empty), so no dependency changes. Resolved runtime versions are Spring Boot 4.1.2 and tools.jackson databind 3.1.7 from `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`. No NVD match ran: dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -F dependencyCheck build.gradle` empty), a listed standing gap.
Scope of evidence: IntelliJ oracle not connected, so route and reference claims rest on grep, the weaker basis. `./gradlew test` was not run in this review; behavior was judged from source.
